name: Naama
title: Solomon's Ammonite wife
summary: Naama was an Ammonite woman who became one of King Solomon's wives. She is best known as the mother of Rehoboam, who succeeded Solomon as king over Judah. Her foreign origin is mentioned as part of the broader issue of Solomon's foreign wives that led him away from the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Naama was one of the many foreign women King Solomon took as wives, including Ammonite women, which was contrary to God's command.

keyEvents.title: Mother of Rehoboam
keyEvents.description: Naama gave birth to Rehoboam, who would become the next king of Judah after Solomon. Her Ammonite background is explicitly mentioned in connection with Rehoboam's reign.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's apostasy through foreign gods
keyEvents.description: Solomon's foreign wives, including Ammonite women like Naama, turned his heart away from the Lord to worship foreign gods, among them Milcom, the god of the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: Rehoboam becomes king in Judah
keyEvents.description: After Solomon's death, Rehoboam son of Naaman became king, and Naaman is mentioned as his mother. She is identified as the Ammonite woman.

keyEvents.title: The Division of the Kingdom under Rehoboam
keyEvents.description: Rehoboam son of Naaman ruled so harshly that the northern tribes broke away and formed their own kingdom under Jeroboam, leaving only Judah and Benjamin under David's dynasty.
